skill.name: bruno-api
skill.description: Generate API endpoint documentation from Bruno (.bru) files by mapping requests to Django REST Framework or Django Ninja backend code.
skill.summary: Create line-referenced API docs from Bruno requests and Django backend code.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: All static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks in documentation text. The skill describes reading Bruno files, searching Django code, and optionally writing generated documentation, with no evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Markdown inline code was flagged as Ruby or shell backtick execution.
remediation.suggestion: No security code change is required. Authors may avoid ambiguous backtick-heavy prose if scanner noise becomes a publishing problem.

remediation.issue: The skill can write generated documentation to a user supplied output path.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before writing files and keep output paths inside the active workspace.

static_findings.snippet: - A path to a single Bruno file (usually `*.bru`), OR
- `--scan <dir>` to analyze all `.bru` files under a directory.
- `--dry-run` – produce an analysis plan only (no deep codebase search).
- `--output <path>` – write the generated markdown documentation to a file.
- Which `.bru` file(s) to analyze.
- Whether they want `--dry-run` or full documentation.
- `# <Endpoint Name>`
- ``<METHOD> <URL Pattern>``
- `## Overview`
- `## Request` (headers + params/body with types/validation)
- `## Response` (success example + common error cases)
- `## Implementation Details` (URL config + view + serializer/schema; always with `file.py:line`)
- `## Business Logic` (step-by-step, include side effects like tasks/external calls)
- `## Frontend Integration` (TypeScript types + call example + React Query hook example)
- `## Testing` (Bruno tests + edge cases + required fixtures/data)
- `## Notes` (perf considerations, related endpoints, rollout notes)
- `[BLOCKING]` – cannot locate the endpoint implementation or critical auth/permission logic.
- `[SHOULD_FIX]` – documentation gaps due to missing/incomplete source details (e.g., response shape
- `[NOTE]` – optional improvements, related endpoints, refactors, or performance observations.
For each `.bru` file:
- If the URL starts with `/api/v2/`:
- Check `dashboardapp/v2_urls.py`.
- Check `dashboardapp/views/v2/` for the view/viewset.
- If the URL starts with `/api/v2/pulse/`:
- Check `pulse_iq/api/` for Django Ninja routers/endpoints.
- Search app-level `urls.py` modules for the path prefix.
- If needed, `Grep` for a distinctive path segment from the Bruno URL.
- View / ViewSet class and handler method (`list`, `retrieve`, `create`, custom actions).
Always record code references with line numbers (`path/to/file.py:123`).
- When you’re unsure, be explicit about assumptions and mark with `[SHOULD_FIX]`.
### Step 5 — Handle `--output` and `--scan`
- If `--scan <dir>`:
- Find all `.bru` files recursively under that directory.
- If no `--output` is provided, return docs in the response (grouped by file).
- If `--output <path>` is provided:
--path plugins/bruno-api/skills/bruno-api`.
- Use `$skill bruno-api` to invoke.
- Install via `/plugin install bruno-api@diversiotech`.

content.value_statement: Bruno API collections often drift from backend behavior. This skill maps .bru requests to Django or Ninja code and produces endpoint documentation with references.
actual_capabilities: Parses single Bruno files or scans directories for multiple .bru files.
Extracts HTTP methods, URLs, headers, query parameters, path parameters, and request bodies.
Maps endpoints to Django REST Framework views, serializers, permissions, and queryset filtering.
Maps Django Ninja routes to routers, endpoint functions, schemas, auth, and tenant scoping.
Generates markdown documentation with implementation references and severity notes.
Can return documentation in chat or write it to a chosen output path.
limitations: It expects Django REST Framework, Django Ninja, or similar project conventions.
It needs readable Bruno files and backend source files in the workspace.
It may mark gaps when response shapes or auth behavior are unclear.
It does not execute API requests or verify live server behavior.

use_cases.title: Document an Existing Endpoint
use_cases.description: Turn one Bruno request into a backend-linked endpoint document with request, response, auth, and implementation details.

use_cases.title: Review API Coverage
use_cases.description: Scan a directory of Bruno files and identify documentation gaps across multiple backend endpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare Frontend Integration Notes
use_cases.description: Generate endpoint guidance that includes request contracts, response expectations, and frontend integration examples.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Bruno File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bruno-api on api/users/get-user.bru and return the documentation in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dry Run Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Check the expected route search before full documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bruno-api with --dry-run for api/accounts/update-profile.bru. Show where you will inspect the Django implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a Bruno Directory
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate documentation for a collection of endpoint files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bruno-api with --scan api/bruno/admin. Group the generated endpoint documentation by Bruno file.

prompt_templates.title: Write Linked Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with a target output file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bruno-api with --scan api/bruno/pulse --output docs/api/pulse-endpoints.md. Include auth, tenant filtering, and code references.

output_examples.input: A user asks for documentation for one Bruno endpoint file.
output_examples.output: A markdown endpoint document with overview, request fields, response behavior, implementation references, business logic, testing notes, and gaps.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a dry run on a Bruno request.
output_examples.output: A short plan listing the endpoint summary, likely Django files, documentation sections, and expected implementation complexity.

output_examples.input: A user scans a directory of Bruno files.
output_examples.output: Grouped endpoint documentation for each file, with blocking notes when the backend route or permission logic cannot be found.

best_practices: Run a dry run first when the endpoint route is hard to locate.
Keep Bruno files and backend source code in the same workspace.
Review generated assumptions before publishing documentation to other teams.
anti_patterns: Do not use it when the backend source code is unavailable.
Do not treat generated examples as live API test results.
Do not write output files outside the active project workspace.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a Bruno .bru file or a directory passed with --scan.

faq.question: Which backend frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Django REST Framework and Django Ninja conventions.

faq.question: Can it generate documentation for many endpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. Use --scan to process every .bru file under a directory.

faq.question: Can it write documentation to a file?
faq.answer: Yes. Use --output with a target path and review the path before writing.

faq.question: Does it verify live API responses?
faq.answer: No. It documents behavior from Bruno files and backend source code.

faq.question: What happens when implementation details are unclear?
faq.answer: It marks unclear areas with blocking, should-fix, or note labels.
